info.title: Universal VPS Root Shell
info.description: One authenticated action gives the model a general-purpose root shell on the remote VPS. The model can use the host's existing capabilities, install additional packages, runtimes or CLIs when needed, create scripts, manage files and services, call remote APIs, and compose arbitrary non-interactive workflows that the server can execute. Named tools are examples, not a capability boundary.

post.summary: Execute an arbitrary root shell workflow on the remote VPS
post.description: Universal host execution primitive. Runs a command or multiline shell script with /bin/bash -lc as root on the real VPS, not in a repository sandbox. It may inspect or change the operating system, install any required software or CLI through available package managers or installers, read/write files anywhere root can access, build and run programs, manage services and processes, use credentials already configured on the server, call APIs and cloud platforms, and chain these abilities into arbitrary workflows. Do not infer a fixed tool allowlist from examples: if a required capability is missing, the shell may install or bootstrap it first. Commands are non-interactive, output is capped, and execution is timeout-limited.

command.description: Any shell command or multiline script to execute with /bin/bash -lc. Multiple dependent steps may be combined into one script.

workdir.description: Optional absolute or relative host working directory. Defaults to /root. It is not restricted to a repository workspace.

stdin.description: Optional standard input passed to the command. Useful for non-interactive CLI input, scripts, payloads and file content.

timeout_seconds.description: Optional timeout for this call. It may shorten, but cannot exceed, the server-side COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS limit.

200.description: Workflow finished. Inspect exit_code, stdout, stderr, timed_out and truncated before deciding the next step.

500.description: The shell could not be started or the requested workdir is unavailable.
